criteria.evidence: All five guided sections plus Sources and Agent intent (ICE) are substantive: e.g. Outputs "one error per bad link, naming the node, the field and the value: \"points at work\" for a bare issue number, \"points at a business intent\" or \"points at a domain\" for those ids, and \"not in the spine\" for any other id"; eight Given/When/Then criteria; Out of scope names fn-724, cap-718, cap-720, cap-721, fn-597, fn-726.

"every mix is allowed, because work across capabilities often needs a piece of another capability"; "It is an error and not a warning, unlike a missing link, because a missing link is a gap the model fills as it grows, while a loop is a link that is present and can never come true"; "Slices and epics ... are renamed in the same change so one field name means one thing."

Rules are discrete bullets; acceptance is Given/When/Then, e.g. "Given a spine where a functionality's need names a Story issue number instead of a node id, when the linter runs, then it fails with an error naming that link." The function is stated as behavior, not a user story.

Parent says only: "the 'needs' and 'identified by' links ... in any mix, and the check that each points at a real node, and the rename of the spine field `depends_on` to `needs`." Child adds the id-prefix rule ("`cap-<n>` ... `fn-<n>` ... a bare issue number, such as `725` or `#725`, is reported as 'points at work'"), the one-error-per-link rule, loop detection, and the schema version 2 -> 3 transition with warning vs error.

What: "A capability or functionality can need, and be identified by, another capability or functionality — any mix. Never on work". Why: "it is the only link that sets an order of work, and the ready check reads it" and "The rename makes the field say what the ontology says". Edges: Out of scope lists the ready answer (fn-724), plan needs (cap-718/720/721), business intent links (fn-597) and domain links (fn-726).
